question: My oven won't light. I've tried replacing the igniter, but it still won't turn on. What could be the problem?
answer: To troubleshoot an oven that won't light, check for any signs of damage or wear on the igniter and verify it's properly connected to the oven's wiring. Also, check for any blockages in the igniter's airflow and clean the igniter's electrodes. If the issue persists, check the oven's thermostat for proper function and the igniter control module for any issues. If none of these steps resolve the issue, replace the igniter.
steps: Remove the oven range top to access the igniter
Check for any signs of damage or wear on the igniter
Verify the igniter is properly connected to the oven's wiring
Check for any blockages in the igniter's airflow
Check the oven's thermostat for proper function
Check for any issues with the oven's igniter control module
Verify the oven is working properly
Check for any error codes on the oven's display
safety_info: Specific hazard: Electrical shock from improper handling of wires. Precaution: When handling wires, always turn off the power to the oven at the circuit breaker or fuse box and verify the wires are de-energized before working on them.
tips: When cleaning the igniter's electrodes, use a small brush to gently remove any debris or food particles
When checking the oven's thermostat, make sure it's set to the correct temperature range
When replacing the igniter, make sure to properly dispose of the old igniter to avoid any electrical shock hazards
